## Check your understanding

Answer each question before opening it.

**1. A Temporal user asks for Restate's equivalent of an activity. What do you tell them?**

- a) A virtual object
- b) ctx.run(...) inside the handler
- c) A deployment
- d) An awakeable

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**b)** Both are 'a side effect, executed and recorded'. Restate keeps them inline; Temporal keeps them in separate functions.

</details>

**2. Your code is down. Which platform reports errors, and which waits silently?**

- a) Restate reports connection errors; Temporal waits silently on the task queue
- b) Temporal reports errors; Restate waits silently
- c) Both report errors
- d) Both wait silently

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**a)** Push (Restate) means the server tries to call you and records the failure. Pull (Temporal) means work waits until a worker asks for it.

</details>

**3. What's the closest Temporal equivalent of a Restate virtual object?**

- a) A task queue
- b) An entity workflow with signals, updates and queries
- c) A namespace
- d) An activity

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**b)** One long-running workflow per entity, changed by messages and read by queries.

</details>

**4. How does each platform keep in-flight work on compatible code by default?**

- a) Both use patching
- b) Restate pins invocations to their deployment; Temporal needs patched() or Worker Versioning
- c) Neither does anything
- d) Temporal pins; Restate needs patching

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**b)** Restate's deployments are immutable and invocations are pinned. In Temporal any worker may replay any execution unless versioning is configured.

</details>

**5. A prospect runs everything on serverless functions. Which architectural property makes Restate a natural fit?**

- a) It has more SDKs
- b) Push-based invocation plus suspension: functions only run while there's work
- c) It doesn't need idempotency keys
- d) It has no server

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**b)** Restate calls the function when there's work and suspends waiting invocations, so nothing runs (or bills) while waiting.

</details>
